# Calculate your IELTS overall band: averaging and rounding examples

Canonical page: https://nepocore.com/blog/ielts-overall-band-rounding-worked-examples/

By Nepocore. Published 2026-11-05; updated 2026-11-05.

Work through four section scores, .25 and .75 boundaries, and the difference between an overall band and a recipient’s requirements.

## Quick answer

Add the four section bands, divide by four and round to the nearest whole or half band. An average of 7.25 becomes 7.5; 7.75 becomes 8.0. Check section minimums and test requirements separately with the recipient.

## Start with four section bands

The overall calculation uses the awarded Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking band scores. Add them and divide the total by four. Then round the average to the nearest whole or half band. IELTS publishes the rule, including the upward rounding at averages ending in .25 and .75. Nepocore applies that arithmetic and shows both the average and the rounded overall result.

Enter section bands rather than correct-answer counts. A Listening practice result of 30 out of 40 is a raw mark, not a band of 30. Use a suitable raw-score estimate first if you are working from practice questions. Writing and Speaking also need assessed section bands; counting words or rating your confidence cannot supply an official section score.

## Work through an average ending in .25

Take Listening 8.0, Reading 7.5, Writing 7.0 and Speaking 6.5. The sum is 29.0. Dividing by four gives 7.25, which rounds upward to an overall band of 7.5. Keep the average visible until the rounding step so you can explain where the final band came from.

Do not round each section again or round 7.25 to a whole number before applying the rule. Section inputs are already band scores. An extra rounding step can change the result and make a correct calculation look inconsistent. Enter the same four values into the calculator and compare its Average before rounding line with your written arithmetic.

## Compare .75 and other boundaries

For Listening 8.0, Reading 8.0, Writing 7.5 and Speaking 7.5, the total is 31.0 and the average is 7.75. This rounds upward to 8.0. Not every average ends at those boundaries: for example, 6.0, 6.0, 5.5 and 6.0 average 5.875 and round to 6.0.

| L / R / W / S | Average | Overall band |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8.0 / 7.5 / 7.0 / 6.5 | 7.25 | 7.5 |
| 8.0 / 8.0 / 7.5 / 7.5 | 7.75 | 8.0 |
| 7.5 / 7.0 / 6.5 / 7.0 | 7.0 | 7.0 |
| 6.0 / 6.0 / 5.5 / 6.0 | 5.875 | 6.0 |

These are original arithmetic examples, not reported test results or predictions of a learner’s performance. Try changing just one section by half a band to see whether the final overall band changes. A higher average can still round to the same overall band. That is a property of the rounding interval, rather than evidence that improvement in that section has no value.

## Keep overall scores separate from minimum section requirements

Two people can have the same overall band and different section scores. A university, professional body or immigration route may require a particular overall score and separate minimums in one or more sections. The overall number alone does not establish that the full requirement is met.

Check the receiving organization’s current official wording for the test type, section minimums, accepted test versions and result validity. This tool does not read application rules or make an admission or visa decision. If the wording is unclear, resolve it with the recipient rather than treating a rounded total as permission to apply.

## Use practice estimates honestly

Practice raw-score conversions are estimates. The score needed for a band can vary with the test version, and Academic and General Training Reading are not interchangeable scales. Keep the original practice paper and mark scheme alongside any converted score so you know what the estimate refers to.

Use the overall calculator to understand the arithmetic and compare scenarios, then plan study around the actual skills you need to improve. It cannot predict an examiner’s future Writing or Speaking assessment. Nepocore is an independent practice tool, not an IELTS Test Report Form or an official score verification service. The linked IELTS reference is the authority for the published scoring rule.
